correctness.rationale: The full finite spin generator gives an exact three-orbit closed system for pair correlations with strictly positive denominators. The induced rational stationary magnetization variance is algebraically determined and the square-root asymptotics follow by dominant-term expansions with fixed eta>0. Independently solving 54 exact-rational lumped CTMC stationary systems verifies representative small graphs, including both model clocks, but finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Named primary literature establishes clock conventions and generic noisy-voter node-clock second moments, but inspected full texts and Research-record searches found no statement encompassing both directed-edge and vertex-clock exact K_{m,n} variances with their sharp sqrt(n) ratio crossover. Claim is confined to that conjunction, not to pair-moment closure or stochastic voter rules, with explicit residual risk of historical subsumption.
residual_risks: A general noisy-voter pair-coalescence-with-killing formula might specialize to both update protocols and make the evaluated graph-specific crossover more immediate than identified.
The full historical literature is not exhaustively searchable; relevant equivalences or differently named stationary covariance formulas may remain.
Current computations concern normalized stationary magnetization with different per-vertex copying workloads; alternate normalization would change the comparison.

value.rationale: The exact constant 8(1+eta) in the finite graph aspect-ratio crossover determines where two commonly used microscopic clock conventions reverse their ordering in stationary aggregate fluctuations. The result links fixed minority size, sqrt(n) imbalance and balanced graph limits in one natural graph family, is not just a numerical sample or relabeling, and supplies a benchmark for heterogeneous network dynamics; distinct copying workloads are intentionally exposed.
